sources.entry: Standard Notes - Simple and private notes app. Protect your privacy while getting more done. That's Standard Notes. (Demo, Source Code) GPL-3.0 Ruby
Standard Notes - Safe place for your notes, thoughts, and life's work.

summary.one_liner: Standard Notes is an end-to-end encrypted note-taking app for notes, files, and long-term records, with sync across devices and an option to self-host the sync server.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Standard Notes as an end-to-end encrypted note-taking app for syncing notes and files across unlimited devices, with only the user able to read them. Users can register at the hosted web app and download clients for Mac, Windows, Linux, iOS, and Android. The public source code can be used to self-host the web app, which is built into static HTML, JS, and CSS files that can be served over HTTP, for example with Python's http.server. A DEFAULT_SYNC_SERVER environment variable sets the default server used for login and registration. The README also mentions Listed, a companion service for publishing a blog with email newsletters, and a developer extension system.
use_cases: Sync notes across phone and computer
Publish a blog with email newsletters
Store files and long-term personal records securely
Keep work notes private from the service provider
notable: End-to-end encrypted sync, so only the user can read notes
Source code is public and the sync server can be self-hosted
Web app compiles to static files that any web server can host
Clients for Mac, Windows, Linux, iOS, and Android
Listed integration for publishing a blog with newsletters
caveats: Self-hosting steps in the README are brief and the web app is served as static files; no server setup is described in detail
The README does not state whether the hosted service is free beyond saying sync is free and unlimited across devices
keywords: sync notes between phone and laptop
